1. Leave granted.
2. The appellant is the mother-in-law of respondent No.2 seeks to quash the proceeding initiated under Sections 498A, 323, 504 and 506 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (for short, the Act) in case No.347/2022, pending on the file of the Additional Civil Judge, (Junior Division), Court No.21,
Allahabad.

Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The appellants son who is incidentally the husband of respondent No.2 was also arrayed as an accused.
Unfortunately, he is no more as he died of cancer way back in the year 2022.
3. On a perusal of the allegations made against the SWETA BALODI Date: 2024.02.17 13:39:12 IST
Reason:
appellant, we find that there is no sufficient material to implicate her as against her son who is no more.
Added to that, respondent No.2 has also received the retiral benefits of the deceased-husband.

On a query, learned counsel appearing for the appellant submitted that there is no objection by the appellant to receive the monthly Sushila Devi vs State Of U.P. on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/165059751/
1 pensionary amount due, if any, pursuant to the death of her husband in terms of the prevailing rules and regulations.
4. Learned counsel appearing for the appellant submitted that a family member certificate would also be facilitated by saying no objection for the inclusion of the name of respondent No.2.

sentences.text: The said statement is also recorded.
However, it is submitted that insofar as the dispute pertaining to the immovable properties is concerned, the same has to be worked out before the jurisdictional Court.
5. While quashing the proceedings, the aforesaid submissions made by the learned counsel appearing for the appellant stands recorded.

6. Needless to state that the appellant shall comply with the statement made by her counsel on her behalf.
7.

Insofar as the dispute between the parties on the division of immovable properties is concerned,
liberty is given to respondent No.2 to work out the remedy in the manner known to law.
8. Accordingly, the appeal stands allowed by quashing the proceedings pending before the Additional Civil Judge, (Junior Division), Court No.21, Allahabad 9.
